name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,129

clue.text: Last drink — cheers!

blocks.note: first meaning: the call to drain a glass to the bottom, a final swig
second meaning: a toast called out as glasses are raised

explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes it read like a barman's closing call followed by a toast; both halves are meanings of the same drinking phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a toast urging everyone to empty their glasses, so it is both a cheery salute and a final gulp.

clue.text: Poisoner flexed elbow having implanted seed

indicators.note: a flexed limb is bent into a new shape, so the word elbow is bent into a new order
having something implanted means holding it inside, so the seed goes within the other letters

blocks.note: the joint of the arm, taken as written
a pip is the small seed of a fruit such as an apple

explanation.surface: A murderer bends his arm, having planted a seed, as if staging some sinister garden poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The seed is not planted in the middle: it goes in just before the last letter of the rearranged arm joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube used by hunters to fire darts tipped with venom, so it is a weapon that delivers toxin.

clue.text: Digit that’s over eight, first of all

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of every one of the preceding words

blocks.note: the initials of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone counting on their fingers reaches a digit beyond eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Digit covers fingers and toes alike, so a toe is one example of a digit on the foot.

clue.text: Proprietor hugged by grandchildren woken up

indicators.note: being hugged by words means sitting tucked inside them, so the letters lie within the run of the clue
in a down clue up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddling the end of grandchildren and the start of woken

explanation.surface: A landlord is embraced by grandchildren who have just been roused from sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the person who holds title to a business or property, which is the plain sense of the answer.

clue.text: Bold wife in belt, doing that up?

indicators.note: the wife sits in the belt, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn around the waist
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
fastening a belt is buckling it; that refers back to the belt

explanation.surface: A daring wife puts on a belt and asks whether she should fasten it.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside SASH to make S-W-ASH; 'that' in the last part points back to the belt, and what you do to a belt is buckle it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swashbuckling describes daring, swaggering adventurers like pirates of film, so it is a lively synonym for daring.

clue.text: Notices distributed to press

indicators.note: things distributed are spread about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, all seven letters

explanation.surface: Announcements are handed out to journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link word, but it is part of the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Posters are printed bills put up on walls to announce events, so they are public notices.

clue.text: Some ignoramus, a proper idiot!

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a part of their run of letters is wanted

blocks.note: the last letter of ignoramus, then a, then the first letter of proper

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that an ignorant person is a real fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sap is an informal word for a gullible fool, so it means a dimwit.

clue.text: Gardening prep?

blocks.note: surface reading: getting the soil ready by digging before planting
setter's reading: groundwork in any project, named after the digging tool

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the literal gardening picture is a pun on a general term for groundwork.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the dull groundwork done before any task, literally digging with a garden tool before planting.

clue.text: Advert for type of pastry?

blocks.note: first meaning: an exaggerated promotional write-up
second meaning: the light flaky pastry made of many layers

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is a commercial for a particular kind of pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is a flattering promotional blurb, and puff pastry is the flaky layered dough used for vol-au-vents.

clue.text: A canoe I adapted for Pacific region

indicators.note: something adapted is altered to suit, so these letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone modifies a canoe for paddling around the South Seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the name for Australia, New Zealand and the island groups of the central and south Pacific.

clue.text: Club employees

blocks.note: first meaning: a stout stick or cudgel
second meaning: the people working for an organisation

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the workers at a club, but club here is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a long walking stick or cudgel, and the word also names the whole workforce of a firm.

clue.text: Bleeper beginning to provoke dreadful rage

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
dreadful suggests something in a terrible state, so the following word is mangled into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of provoke
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A beeping device going off starts to provoke a terrible temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager is a small radio device that beeps to summon its wearer, hence the nickname bleeper.

clue.text: Dog barking at grenade

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, and the following letters go mad into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hound yaps at an explosive device.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the dog's noise, but in British slang it also means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a very large breed of hound, so it is one example of a canine.

clue.text: Paid close attention to extraordinary deed by that man

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the usual order, so the letters of the following word are rearranged
by means next to, so one part sits beside the other

blocks.note: the pronoun for a male person
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone took careful note of a remarkable act performed by a particular man.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to take notice of advice or a warning, so the past tense means listened carefully.

clue.text: Hunter, marksman from the southeast?

indicators.note: the archer comes from a region, so the region is placed before him

blocks.note: SE is the compass abbreviation
a marksman with a bow

explanation.surface: A tracker turns out to be a sharpshooter hailing from the south-eastern part of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A searcher is someone who looks for something, much as a hunter seeks out quarry.

clue.text: Converted to supersonic, English jet, say

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters are changed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English aircraft has been upgraded to fly faster than sound, like Concorde.
explanation.walkthrough: Jet looks like an aeroplane, which suits the supersonic picture; here it is the black mineral used in jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet is a black gem-quality stone used in mourning jewellery, so it is one example of a gem.

clue.text: Straight, as might be a nun?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a single word

blocks.note: first meaning: tidy, properly arranged
second meaning: belonging to a religious community of sisters

explanation.walkthrough: A nun is a member of a religious order, which gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Things set straight are neatly arranged, and a nun is a member of a religious community, so both describe her.

clue.text: Couple aboard ship scrubbing the decks, perhaps?

indicators.note: aboard a vessel means inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Noah's ark, the vessel
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A pair of sailors on a vessel spend their time swabbing the decks.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple aboard the ark recalls Noah's animals going in two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: Swabbing decks is a sailor's labour, so someone doing it is busy with the job, an example of being employed.

clue.text: Game with hands — and index finger?

blocks.note: first meaning: a card game played in rounds of dealt cards
second meaning: something used for prodding, as a pointing finger is

explanation.walkthrough: Hands are dealt cards, not body parts, though the finger keeps the body picture going.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a gambling card game, and a forefinger is a jabbing thing, a prodder.

clue.text: Border raised, lifted for student

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means turned upwards, so the letters read from the bottom up

blocks.note: a lip is an edge or rim
something raised is up

explanation.surface: A boundary is put up for the benefit of a schoolchild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border raised' gives LIP UP, and the whole run is then turned over to read PU PIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a child or young person taught at a school, so a learner in a class.

clue.text: Great time for bouncer?

blocks.note: first meaning: as in having a really enjoyable time
second meaning: something that springs back off the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Bouncer suggests a nightclub doorman, but here it is something that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a ball is the idiom for enjoying yourself, and a ball is the round toy that rebounds off floors.

clue.text: Honour a hospital department

blocks.note: taken as written
a ward is a room or section of beds in a hospital

explanation.surface: A medical unit receives a prize for its excellent service.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize or decoration conferred in recognition, which is what an honour is.

clue.text: One politician for every one charge

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Member of Parliament
each means for every one

explanation.surface: Reads like a rule of parliamentary arithmetic: a single member for every single voter.
explanation.walkthrough: The final word is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach a public official is to formally accuse them of misconduct, bringing an accusation.

clue.text: Fit character starting arduous physical training

indicators.note: a character is a letter, and the starting one of each word is the one kept

blocks.note: the initials of the three words

explanation.surface: A person of fit disposition begins a gruelling exercise regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable or appropriate, as in a fitting remark, the adjectival sense of fit.

clue.text: Get down story

blocks.note: first meaning: recline flat, as on a bed
second meaning: a falsehood, a fib

explanation.walkthrough: Story is used in the sense of a tall tale told to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline flat is one sense of the verb, and an untruth or fib is the noun sense.

clue.text: A ruler got mistaken for governor

indicators.note: something mistaken is wrong, so the letters are put in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch was confused with a state governor.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruler and governor look like a pair of politicians; governor is a mechanical device here.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor in engineering is a device that controls speed or flow, which is what a regulator does.
